papers.title: Understanding of Co-N3-X1 (X = N, S, Se, and Te) Moieties for the Oxygen Reduction Reaction
papers.abstract: Abstract Controlled synthesis of single-atom catalysts (SACs) with different first coordination shells offers an ideal platform for elucidating structure–performance relationships in SACs. Herein, a series of SACs with a well-defined configuration of Co-N3X1-C (X = N, S, Se, and Te) were synthesized for the oxygen reduction reaction (ORR). Theoretical calculations reveal that the negative value of the integrated crystal orbital Hamilton population for the Co(dz2+ dyz)–O(p) interaction provides a better correlation than the d-band center with the adsorption energy of oxygen species. In situ X-ray absorption near-edge structure analyses indicate that the adsorption of oxygen species on the catalysts is consistent with the calculated OH* adsorption trend. The energy gap between the highest occupied molecular orbital of SACs and the lowest unoccupied molecular orbital of O2 shows a linear relationship with the Bader charge related to O2 activation. Theoretical calculations and in situ Raman spectroscopy indicate that Co-N3S1-C realizes a better balance of O2 activation and *OH desorption, enabling it to exhibit the optimal catalytic activity with an E1/2 of 0.90 V and the largest turnover frequency value of 21.5 s–1. Furthermore, a liquid zinc-air battery with a Co-N3S1-C cathode delivers a power density of 255.4 mW cm–2, which is higher than that of the battery with a Pt/C + IrO2 cathode (196.6 mW cm–2) and most of the Fe- and Co-based electrocatalysts as cathodes reported in the literature. These findings could shed insight on the theoretical exploration of SACs and the heterogenization of homogeneous catalysts.

papers.title: Coupling O2 Activation with Proton Capture Boosts Carbon Nitride Fixed-Bed Flow Photosynthesis of Hydrogen Peroxide
papers.abstract: Abstract Practical H2O2 photoproduction via the 2e ORR by polymeric carbon nitride (CN) is hindered by insufficient surface reaction kinetics, limitations in continuous reaction, and extra H2O2/catalyst separation. This work engineered fixed-bed CN networks with oxophilic Ni nanoparticles and proton-affinitive anthraquinone moieties, which enhanced the catalyst’s O2 adsorption/activation and proton capture capability. Besides, due to the electronic delocalization and extended π–π conjugation system, they imparted the catalyst with extended light absorption and improved charge separation. The as-synthesized photocatalyst demonstrated a 12.7-fold enhancement of H2O2 yield in flowing water, which reaches 3.6 mmol m–2 h–1 (1362 μmol g–1 h–1), outperforming most reported CN-based catalysts. Under natural sunlight irradiation, 581.8 μmol H2O2 was produced in 9 h using a 12 cm × 8.5 cm photocatalyst sheet. The practical application was exemplified by efficient on-site flow photo-Fenton degradation of organic contaminants with >90% degradation in 1.5 h. Electronic studies and local reactant enrichment investigation revealed that the adsorbed O2 at the Ni site and protons at AQ proceed to generate H2O2 upon participation of photogenerated electrons via the two-step 1e ORR process with high selectivity. This work demonstrates a successful surface chemistry design of fixed-bed CN networks for efficient continuous-flow photoproduction of H2O2 with facile separation.

Porous Organic Frameworks for Overall Photosynthesis H2O2
papers.abstract: Solar‐to‐H 2 O 2 conversion represents one of the most promising avenues for sustainable development, while overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via the dual pathways of simultaneous ORR and WOR holds significant scientific value. This review first systematically summarizes the recent advancements of porous organic frameworks (POFs) for overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis. Starting with a concise overview of the fundamental principles of H 2 O 2 photosynthesis via ORR and WOR, as well as dual‐channel H 2 O 2 photosynthesis, the evaluation protocols and key factors are briefly discussed. Thereafter, the advantages, development, and typical design strategies of POFs for this process are summarized. Subsequently, various smart POFs for dual‐pathway photosynthesis H 2 O 2 are introduced. In the past year alone, diverse molecular design strategies have driven continuous gains across all performance metrics, with records reaching a H 2 O 2 production rate of 17.25 mmol·g −1 h −1 , an accumulated concentration of 82.3 mM, an AQY of 40%, and an SCC efficiency of 4.7%. Last but not least, conclusions, challenges, and long‐term outlooks of this field are revealed with a focus on POFs design, computer‐assist, H 2 O 2 decomposition, and mechanism investigations. This review aims to offer in‐depth insights and guidelines for POFs in efficient overall H 2 O 2 photosynthesis.

Entropy Engineering Accelerates High-Temperature Oxygen Evolution Reaction Rate via Spin Manipulation
papers.abstract: Abstract The high-temperature oxygen evolution reaction (OER) activity is closely correlated to the spin state of transition metals in perovskite anodes. However, the roles of entropy engineering in modulating the spin state and influencing high-temperature OER kinetics remain poorly understood. Herein, we demonstrate that entropy engineering of La0.7Sr0.3FeO3−δ to (SmNdPrLaBaSrCa)FeO3−δ (SNPLBSCF) induces a transition of B-site Fe species from high-spin to low-spin states. This transition enhances the d–p hybridization of Fe–O bonds, lowers the energy barriers for electron transfer and oxygen ion migration, and finally accelerates the high-temperature OER kinetics. Consequently, the SNPLBSCF anode in a solid oxide electrolysis cell (SOEC) achieves a current density of 3.64 A·cm–2 at 800 °C and 1.6 V, outperforming most reported anodes. This work not only provides fundamental insights into the spin state-activity relationships of perovskite oxides but also offers a viable strategy for the rational design of highly efficient SOEC anodes through entropy engineering.
